policy_definitions.current: Existing Cipher.encryptBlocks/decryptBlocks decomposition into 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, and scalar blocks.
policy_definitions.pad64: Zero a 64-block local buffer, copy all n valid inputs, run the existing 64-block sliced kernel, and copy only n outputs back.
policy_definitions.next_power: Zero/copy a local buffer rounded to 4, 8, 16, 32, or 64 blocks; use the existing matrix kernel below 64 or sliced kernel at 64.
policy_definitions.pad_small_tail: Keep current decomposition for the multiple-of-four prefix. A final two/three-block tail uses a zero-padded four-block matrix call; a one-block tail remains scalar.

measurement.lengths: Every integer from 1 through 63, encryption and decryption.
measurement.buffer_setup: All padding, zero initialization, and input/output copies occur inside the timed policy call on every iteration.
measurement.untimed_setup: Cipher initialization and resetting inputs between samples.
measurement.order: Alternate policy order on successive paired samples.
measurement.state: Independent blocks each depend on their previous result; every policy checksum must match.

correctness.random_policy_validation: Eight independent keys, every length 0..63, four starting offsets preserving only 16-byte alignment, all four policies, both arbitrary plaintext encryption and arbitrary ciphertext decryption.
correctness.guards: Compare entire surrounding 72-block arrays against an independent scalar oracle to check both outputs and untouched prefixes/suffixes.

selection_note: The selected rule matches clear winners for both operations. Cases within three percent of current behavior retain the simpler current path. Equivalent next-power and pad64 cases above 32 are classified as pad64.

narrow_32_control.description: A new YMM byte-sliced 32-block kernel was correct and faster than matrix32, but nearly tied simply padding the existing ZMM64 kernel; avoid a new production architecture for that small difference.
narrow_32_control.feature_requirement_for_narrow: GFNI/AVX-512/VBMI plus AVX-512VL; the padded existing 64-block path requires no new VL condition.
narrow_32_control.correctness: All 21 tests passed, including RFC vector in all 32 lanes, random plaintext/arbitrary ciphertext, all linear basis vectors, alignment offsets and mixed tail boundaries through 129 blocks.

scope: Measurements support this tested CPU and compiler, not a physical optimum or universal cross-CPU thresholds. The two main padding matrices contain 252 length/operation records (126 each), plus separate narrow-kernel controls.
first_matrix_selected_rule: After processing complete 64-block chunks: if n >= 21 and n != 24, pad to 64 and return.
Otherwise, process a complete 16-block prefix when present.
For remaining n >= 10 and n != 12, pad to 16 and return.
Otherwise, process a complete 8-block prefix when present.
For remaining n >= 5, pad to 8 and return.
Otherwise, process a complete 4-block prefix when present.
For remaining n >= 2, pad to 4 and return.
A final one-block tail stays scalar; an empty tail is a no-op.
candidate_rule_after_additional_existing: For a remaining single block, use the single-block kernel. Zero blocks are a no-op.
For remaining lengths 2..24, choose the smallest multiple of four: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, or 24. Existing generic GFNI kernels instantiate group counts 1..6.
For exact selected widths, call that kernel directly. Otherwise zero a local buffer sized to that width, copy valid inputs in, process the padded batch, and copy valid outputs back.
For remaining lengths 25..63, pad to the existing 64-block sliced kernel.
This candidate is supported by this CPU study; cross-machine replication and production integration are tracked separately.

additional_existing_kernel_sizes.description: The existing GFNI implementation accepts any group count. Add measured 12-, 20-, 24-, and 28-block instances without adding a new algorithm or ISA requirement.
additional_existing_kernel_sizes.greedy: Process a 16-block prefix, then pad the remaining 5..7 blocks to 8. Use the earlier adaptive choices below that and pad64 from length25 upward.
additional_existing_kernel_sizes.multiple4: Round up to the next multiple of four through width32; instantiate GFNI group counts 1..8. Use pad64 above32.
additional_existing_kernel_sizes.correctness: All 23 tests passed again, including eight keys, every length0..63, four alignment offsets, arbitrary encryption/decryption, and surrounding guards for every policy.
additional_existing_kernel_sizes.finding: 12-, 20-, and 24-block instances improve throughput beyond power-of-two padding and composite kernels. The 28-block instance did not give a consistent gain over padded64, so it is excluded from the simpler candidate.
additional_existing_kernel_sizes.setup: Each padded buffer is zero-initialized at its selected width, and all copies remain inside the timed call.
